setup_summary.text: Q3 2026 (reported Oct 29–30) revenue was $201.94B, up 12.1% YoY. Operating income was $28.08B, up 61% with a 13.9% margin versus 9.7% a year earlier. Management called 13.9% its highest operating margin ever. Q3 2025 carried a $2.5B FTC settlement and $1.8B of severance.

AWS is the engine. Q3 sales were $45.98B, up 39%. Operating income was $17.77B, a 38.7% margin versus $11.43B a year ago. It was the sixth straight quarter of acceleration, with $3.8B added sequentially. Backlog (remaining performance obligations) was $578B versus $244B at year-end, including the OpenAI (+$100B over 8 years) and Anthropic (>$100B over 10 years) expansions.

Net income fell 2.4% to $20.69B and diluted EPS fell to $1.89 from $1.95, despite the 61% rise in operating income. Other income (expense), net swung to -$703M from +$10.19B (prior-year Anthropic mark-ups). Interest expense rose to $1.69B from $538M. Below-the-line items are now the main source of EPS volatility.

The cash picture is the bear anchor. Q3 operating cash flow of $42.4B compared with $77.3B of property and equipment purchases, so simple Q3 free cash flow was about -$34.8B versus +$0.4B a year earlier. Company-defined trailing-twelve-month free cash flow was -$42.4B versus +$14.8B.

Leverage has stepped up sharply. Long-term debt (ex-current portion) was $173.1B at 9/30/26 versus $65.6B at year-end, helped by a $25B July notes issue, £4.3B of sterling notes and a $17.5B term loan drawn in September. Cash and equivalents fell to $55.8B. Total contractual commitments rose to $883.6B from $439.7B. A secured supplier Loan Facility of up to about $80B is available from Q1 2027.

The setup into the Q4 print (due 2027-02-03) is a stock that sold off on expectations. Q3 EPS of $1.89 missed the $1.96 LSEG consensus and revenue narrowly missed $202.31B. AWS growth of 39% fell short of some buy-side hopes (BofA cited expectations as high as 42%). Shares fell nearly 7% premarket and were down about 2% intraday on Oct 30. Most analysts kept Buy/Overweight ratings but trimmed targets.

The next report is fiscal Q4 2026 on 2027-02-03 after the close. Consensus is revenue of $249.46B and EPS of $2.50. The last eight reports averaged a ±6.2% closing move. Amazon beat EPS once and missed three times over the last four quarters, with an average surprise of -1.5%. Whisper EPS and options-implied move are not yet available.

last_reported.text: Q4 2025 net sales were $256.07B (derived as FY2025 less nine months). Q3 2026 net sales were $201.94B, +12.1% YoY.

consensus.text: Consensus is $249.46B (+16.9% YoY), above the top of the guided range. Coverage dated Oct 30 cited a lower ~$244.5B consensus. The two figures differ and the discrepancy is unresolved.

view.text: Guidance is $240.0–247.0B (+12% to +16%) including about 60bp of FX headwind. Consensus of $249.46B needs a beat of the high end by about $2.5B. Q3 revenue landed at the top of its guided range ($197–202B), so model the upper half of guidance (~$245–247B) and treat $249B as a stretch. Prime Day timing no longer distorts the comparison in Q4.

last_reported.text: Q4 2025 operating income was $25.0B. Q3 2026 was $28.08B (13.9% margin).

consensus.text: Coverage cites a pre-print consensus of ~$39.59B, near the top of the guided range (this is a coverage-cited figure, not verified).

view.text: Guidance is $28.5–33.5B, a $5B-wide range around a ~$31.0B midpoint. Amazon exceeded its prior Q3 range ($22.5–26.5B, delivering $28.1B), so a beat of the midpoint is plausible. The CFO said most Amazon Leo costs stay expensed in Q4, and fuel and line-haul inflation is a bit higher than in Q3. Guidance excludes energy-derivative remeasurements (a +$91M gain in Q3).

last_reported.text: Q4 2025 diluted EPS was $1.95 (derived). Q3 2026 was $1.89.

view.text: Consensus looks demanding. With Q3-like net interest (about -$0.6B), a ~23% tax rate (Q3: $6.18B on $26.9B pre-tax) and ~10.93B diluted shares, operating income of $31–33.5B converts to roughly $2.15–2.30 per share before any investment marks. $2.50 therefore needs several billion dollars of pre-tax non-operating gains, or an operating beat above the range. The Q3 mark-up was only $39M. Interest expense should rise from $1.69B because the September term loan and sterling notes carry a full quarter. This is the key EPS risk.

last_reported.text: Q3 2026 AWS sales were $45.98B (+39%, 39.3% per management), a $184B annualized run rate, up $3.8B QoQ.

view.text: Q4 2025 AWS sales were about $35.6B (FY2025 $128.7B less nine months $93.1B). A repeat of the Q3 sequential add of $3.8B gives about $49.8B, or roughly +40% YoY. A sequential add below about $3.5B would show growth slipping back below 39%. No AWS consensus was found. Management said capacity additions are uneven by quarter and gave no Q4 capacity figure.

last_reported.text: Q3 2026 AWS operating margin was 38.7%, with AWS segment D&A of $9.23B versus $5.65B a year ago.

view.text: Management declined to guide. It cited efficiency gains and custom chips, but said AI mix (lower margins) and component pricing (memory) are headwinds, and that margins will fluctuate with the pace of investment. Depreciation is growing faster than revenue (+63% versus +39%), so margins in the mid-to-high 30s are a reasonable range. Citi cited the potential to hold the mid-to-high 30s.

last_reported.text: Q3 2026 advertising was $19.64B, up 12% ex-FX, held back by the Prime Day shift (850bp sequential impact), no NBA in Q3 and lapping the Q3 2025 search-program change.

view.text: Management expects Q4 growth in the high teens. On Q4 2025 advertising of about $21.3B (FY2025 $68.6B less nine months $47.3B), 18% growth implies roughly $25B. Q4 has the NBA on Prime launch and no Prime Day distortion, so the bridge is plausible but untested. A reading below ~16% would be a clear negative.

last_reported.text: Q3 cash capex was $75.9B (purchases of property and equipment $77.26B gross). Nine-month cash capex was $172.2B. Q3 free cash flow was about -$34.8B.

view.text: The ~$264B full-year cash capex guide less $172.2B year to date implies only about $48B in Q4, well below Q3's $75.9B. Either the guide is conservative or spend will be pushed into 2027, which management said will be 'meaningfully' higher. Nine-month unpaid property and equipment rose $21.5B, so payables timing is flattering cash outflows. Expect Q4 free cash flow to be less negative than Q3 on cadence, with large 2027 spending still ahead.

last_reported.text: Q3 interest expense was $1.69B (versus $538M), and cash paid for interest on debt was $1.17B. Proceeds from long-term debt were $48.1B in Q3.

view.text: Interest expense should rise again in Q4. The $17.5B term loan and £4.3B notes were drawn in September, and management expects additional financing in 2026. The ~$80B secured Loan Facility starts Q1 2027. Watch for Q4 debt issuance and any capitalized-interest offset.

last_reported.text: Q3 North America sales were $112.85B (+6%) with a 7.7% margin. International sales were $43.11B (+8% ex-FX) with a 3.7% margin. Paid units rose 12% and shipping costs rose 11% (8% ex fuel and line-haul).

view.text: Q3 growth was held back about 400bp by the Prime Day shift, which does not recur in Q4. Fuel and line-haul inflation is a little higher in Q4, partly offset by an FBA fuel surcharge. Expect retail growth to re-accelerate on the easier comparison. Margin direction depends on holiday cost to serve, Leo expense and the quick-commerce rollout.

since_filing.text: Oct 30 market reaction: AMZN fell nearly 7% premarket and traded about 2% lower later in the session. It was reported about 16% below its high by Oct 31. The sell-off was attributed to AWS growth below elevated expectations, soft Q4 guide optics and negative free cash flow. Consensus price target is $328.48 against a $240.35 price.

Post-print analyst actions were mostly target trims with ratings kept positive. Morgan Stanley cut to $335 from $350, Wells Fargo to $326 from $329, BofA to $317 from $320, Goldman to $370 from $375 and TD Cowen to $340 from $350. UBS raised to $352 from $348 and BMO to $390 from $380. Barclays ($365), JPMorgan ($365), Citi ($350), Deutsche ($325) and Bernstein ($320) held. Bernstein called advertising growth weak.

The Q4 guide is seen as light at the center versus coverage-cited expectations. Revenue guidance of $240–247B has a $243.5B midpoint versus a ~$244.5B consensus cited in coverage. Operating income guidance has a ~$31.0B midpoint versus ~$32.99B expected. Current consensus data (revenue $249.46B) is higher than the coverage figure, so the benchmark is unclear.

Peer read-across: Microsoft reported Azure +48% (about $33.2B) and commercial RPO +73% to about $677B. It guided Azure +49–50% in constant currency for its next quarter. AWS at 39% growth is below Azure's rate but on a larger base, which sharpens the competitive-share debate.

Retail and consumer read-across: Walmart's eCommerce grew 23% in its July quarter and its advertising is growing quickly. Walmart's holiday survey (Oct 28) found affordability is the top stressor for 43.8% of U.S. shoppers, and a Yahoo Finance piece (Oct 30) points to value-seeking holiday spending. Walmart+ launched in Mexico on Oct 29. This points to a promotional, price-competitive holiday backdrop.
Management's Q3 call remarks contain no figure on Q4 AWS capacity additions, 2027 capex, or per-household uplift from perishables checkout, so these remain open items for the Q4 call.

key_debates.question: Is AWS acceleration (39.3%) strong enough to support the capex build, and can it exceed 40%?

bull.text: AWS accelerated for a sixth straight quarter, with the fastest growth in nearly five years on a $184B run rate. Backlog of $578B is growing triple digits and AI revenue is growing triple digits. Management sees growth above 40% in 2027 and 2028. Bedrock token volume grew about 17x, and revenue commitments for Trainium and Graviton each rose more than 20x year over year.

bear.text: The market wanted more: Bank of America noted investor expectations had reached as high as 42% against 39% growth, and an analyst on the call pointed out that quarter-over-quarter growth slowed (AWS added $3.8B sequentially). The 10-Q discusses the $578B backlog alongside the OpenAI (+$100B) and Anthropic (>$100B) expansions, though it does not say how much of the backlog they represent. Amazon has also invested $50B in OpenAI preferred stock and $10B in Anthropic preferred stock, and has a $20B Anthropic facility. That raises concentration and circularity questions.

key_debates.what_settles_it: Q4 AWS revenue versus the ~$49–50B needed for ~40% growth, the sequential dollar add, backlog growth and any disclosure of backlog concentration among AI labs.

key_debates.question: Can Amazon fund the capex and does return on invested capital justify it?

bull.text: Management says the plan is fundable, break-even on infrastructure is moving left (shorter), and custom silicon gives structural cost advantages. Operating cash flow rose 19% to $42.4B in Q3 and cash plus marketable securities were $114.2B.

bear.text: Q3 free cash flow was -$34.8B and TTM free cash flow was -$42.4B. Debt more than doubled to $173.1B in nine months. Commitments total $883.6B, including $164.9B of leases not yet commenced. 2027 capex will 'meaningfully' exceed the ~$220B of 2026, and an ~$80B secured loan facility starts in 2027.

key_debates.what_settles_it: A 2027 capex framework, Q4 free cash flow and financing mix, interest cost trajectory and AWS incremental margins as depreciation scales.

key_debates.question: How much of EPS is quality earnings versus mark-to-market gains?

bull.text: Operating income rose 61% to $28.1B at a record 13.9% margin, and Q4 guidance ($28.5–33.5B) implies year-over-year growth versus $25.0B. North America operating income rose to $8.7B from $4.8B (7.7% margin) and International to $1.6B from $1.2B (3.7% margin).

bear.text: Net income fell 2.4% in Q3 as other income swung to -$703M, and nine-month net income of $113.6B includes $68.4B of other income and $15.2B of discrete tax expense tied to Anthropic mark-ups. Private equity holdings of $143.7B and Anthropic convertible notes of $146.2B are Level 3, and the company says market sensitivities are not practicable to disclose. Consensus Q4 EPS of $2.50 compares with Q3 diluted EPS of $1.89.

key_debates.what_settles_it: Q4 other income (expense), the tax rate, any new Anthropic or OpenAI financing-round marks and whether the sell side treats the marks as excluded from consensus.

key_debates.question: Is retail growth durable and is advertising re-accelerating?

bull.text: Paid units grew 12%, YTD units are up nearly 15%, cost to serve is on track to fall for a fourth year, and robotics is scaling (over 1 million robots). The Prime Day shift cost Q3 about 400bp of growth. Advertising is guided to the high teens in Q4.

bear.text: North America grew only 6% and advertising was 12% in Q3, which Bernstein called weak. Fuel and line-haul inflation is higher in Q4. Competitors such as Walmart are growing eCommerce 23%, and consumers are value-seeking, which could force promotion.

key_debates.what_settles_it: Q4 advertising growth (high teens or not), North America growth after the Prime Day normalization, shipping cost per unit and the holiday margin.

scenarios.name: bull

description.text: AWS grows ~40% or more, with sequential adds of $3.8B or more (~$49.8B+). Revenue lands at the top of guidance or above ($247B+, close to $249B consensus). Operating income reaches the high end ($33B+). Advertising returns to the high teens and management gives credible 2027 capex-to-return framing. Mark-ups lift EPS toward the $2.50 consensus.

triggers: AWS Q4 revenue of about $50B or more
Positive mark-ups to Anthropic or OpenAI stakes in Q4

scenarios.name: base

description.text: Revenue comes in around $245–247B (upper half of guidance), operating income lands near the midpoint-to-high end ($31–34B, given Amazon's record of beating its range), AWS grows ~39–40%, and cash capex of about $48B implies free cash flow still negative. EPS is below the $2.50 consensus unless investment marks help, since arithmetic implies roughly $2.15–2.30 from operations at Q3-like net interest.

triggers: Revenue at or slightly above the top of the range
Ads growth in the mid-to-high teens

scenarios.name: bear

description.text: AWS growth slips below 39% as capacity timing or component constraints bite. Operating income lands near or below the $31B midpoint of guidance on fuel and line-haul inflation, component pricing and continued Leo expense. A non-operating loss or no gains leaves EPS well under the $2.50 consensus, after 1 beat and 3 misses in the last 4 quarters. Management signals a meaningful 2027 capex step-up and further financing, which would deepen free cash flow concerns.

triggers: AI-lab valuation write-downs or negative marks
A 2027 capex figure far above Street expectations

claim.text: Leverage and funding risk. Long-term debt more than doubled to $173.1B from $65.6B in nine months, interest expense tripled to $1.69B in Q3, trailing free cash flow is -$42.4B, and long-term debt principal and interest commitments alone total $294.3B. A secured loan facility of up to about $80B is available from Q1 2027. Management says it expects to undertake additional financing in 2026.

AI-lab concentration and valuation risk. The backlog expansions with OpenAI and Anthropic sit alongside Amazon's investments ($50B in OpenAI preferred, Anthropic preferred and notes, and a $20B facility). Private holdings total $143.7B plus $146.2B of Anthropic convertible notes, both Level 3 measurements, and the company says market sensitivities are not practicable. A valuation drop would hit other income, taxes and equity.

AWS margin and cost pressure. Management says AI mix is lower-margin and cites headwinds from component pricing, while AWS depreciation rose 63% year over year ($5.6B to $9.2B) and technology and infrastructure expense grew 20%. Resource and supply volatility, including for memory chips, is a stated forward-looking risk.
Fuel and line-haul inflation is higher in Q4 than in Q3, only partially offset by the FBA fuel surcharge. Leo costs are expensed through Q4 because capitalization is delayed to Q1 2027.

New legal exposure. The FTC and 22 state attorneys general (plus Texas) sued in August 2026 over reserve prices in sponsored-ad auctions, threatening advertising practices. Xockets' ITC investigation (instituted June 2026) seeks injunctive relief against AWS servers using GB200 and GB300 chips. No loss estimates are given, and Q4 guidance excludes legal settlements.

Estimates risk. Consensus revenue ($249.46B) is above the top of guidance ($247B), consensus EPS ($2.50) looks to need non-operating gains, and Amazon has beaten EPS once in the last four quarters with an average surprise of -1.5%. The average closing move is about ±6.2%.

Cloud demand forecasting and AI pricing risk. Microsoft's latest 10-Q warns that overestimating demand can leave infrastructure underutilized and cause impairments, and that AI pricing pressure and high inference and energy costs could hurt margins. Amazon expects about $220B of 2026 cash capex and meaningfully more in 2027, so similar capacity-planning questions are worth watching at AWS. Walmart's eCommerce growth (+23% in its latest quarter) adds retail competition.

questions_for_management.question: What drove the $3.8B sequential AWS add, and how should we think about capacity coming online in Q4 and the next eight quarters versus the 40%+ growth aspiration for 2027–28?

why.text: Analysts pressed on the sequential slowdown. Management said capacity adds vary by quarter but gave no Q4 number, and AWS growth of 39.3% fell short of buy-side hopes as high as 42%.

questions_for_management.question: What share of the $578B backlog comes from OpenAI and Anthropic, how much is chip-related, and how should investors think about the overlap with Amazon's equity investments and financing facility?

why.text: The backlog rose from $244B at year-end 2025 to $578B at September 30, 2026, a period that included the OpenAI (+$100B) and Anthropic (>$100B) expansions, while Amazon invested $50B in OpenAI preferred and committed up to $20B of Anthropic financing.

questions_for_management.question: What is the order of magnitude for 2027 cash capex, how will it be financed (including the ~$80B Loan Facility), and when does free cash flow turn positive?

why.text: 2026 capex is ~$220B and 2027 will meaningfully increase, but no number was given. TTM free cash flow is -$42.4B and debt is $173.1B.

questions_for_management.question: Why does the full-year capex guide imply only about $48B in Q4 versus $75.9B in Q3, and how much of 2026 spend is deferred into 2027 via payables or supplier financing?

why.text: Nine-month cash capex was $172.2B against a ~$220B guide, while unpaid property and equipment rose $21.5B year to date.

questions_for_management.question: How should we model AWS operating margin given AI mix, memory costs and a 63% rise in segment depreciation, and what are the mark-to-market policies and expected Q4 effects for the Anthropic and OpenAI holdings?

why.text: The CFO declined to guide AWS margins and flagged AI mix and component pricing. Other income swung from +$10.2B to -$0.7B, and the $143.7B private holdings are Level 3.

questions_for_management.question: What underlying advertising growth is embedded in the 'high teens' Q4 guide after stripping out NBA and timing, and how will the FTC reserve-price suit affect auction practices?

why.text: Q3 advertising grew 12% ex-FX with several timing anomalies. The FTC and states sued in August over reserve prices in sponsored-ad auctions.

questions_for_management.question: How large are the Q4 Leo costs and the fuel and line-haul headwinds embedded in the $28.5–33.5B operating income range?

why.text: The CFO said most Leo costs continue to be expensed in Q4 and that fuel and line-haul inflation is higher than in Q3, without quantifying either.

data_gaps: No pre-earnings consensus for Q4 AWS revenue, AWS operating margin, advertising revenue, capex or free cash flow was found; the AWS and advertising views here are derived from guidance and management commentary.

Q4 consensus is inconsistent across sources: $249.46B revenue and $2.50 EPS (market-data feed) versus ~$244.5B revenue and ~$32.99B operating income in Oct 30 coverage. The basis and date of each are unverified, and whether consensus EPS includes investment marks is unknown.
The Q4 EPS arithmetic (~$2.15–2.30 from operations) is my estimate using Q3 tax and net interest and ignores any new investment marks, buybacks or tax discretes.
No disclosure of backlog concentration by customer (OpenAI/Anthropic share) or the conversion schedule of the $578B beyond a 6.1-year weighted-average life.
No 2027 capex figure, 2027 financing plan, or Q4 capacity-addition figure was given.

The earnings press release (8-K) was not among the sources; call and 10-Q content were used for Q3 figures. Capex is cited as $75.9B (cash capex net of proceeds, per the 10-Q MD&A) in some outlets and $77.3B (gross purchases of property and equipment) in others; these are different definitions rather than a conflict.
One news summary says Prime Day shifted into Q3 this year from Q2; the 10-Q-era call says the opposite (Prime Day moved into Q2 2026 from Q3 2025). The call is the primary source and was used.
Third-party peer figures (e.g. Google Cloud +103%, $30.7B) came from a single unverified aggregator and look anomalous; they were not used. Microsoft figures are secondhand news reports.
Whisper EPS and options-implied move are unavailable because the report date is 94 days away.
Q4 energy-derivative marks (excluded from guidance; $690M unrealized gains in nine months) and Q4 interest capitalization are not forecastable from the sources.
